title.en: Race to rescue remaining climbers after deadly avalanche in Pakistan
title.zh: 美国登山者遗体被寻回，巴基斯坦雪崩遇难者再添一人

summary.en: The body of a US climber has been recovered in Pakistan, adding to the two other climbers whose bodies were found earlier after an avalanche. Several other climbers remain missing.
summary.zh: 在巴基斯坦，一名美国登山者的遗体被发现，此前已有两名登山者的遗体被寻回，另有数人仍下落不明。

body.en:
Rescue teams in Pakistan are carrying out a second day of search for climbers caught in an avalanche on the world's 12th-highest summit.

Among the seven still missing from the 10-person expedition on Broad Peak, on the border with China, is renowned Nepal-born climber Nirmal Purja.

The operation has expanded with local Pakistani climbers volunteering, together with others from Nepal who have halted their expeditions on nearby K2.

Bad weather has been hampering the search. Pakistani officials say the bodies of three climbers have been recovered.

They have been named as American Mallory Geis, Nadhira Ahmed Abdullah Al Harthy from Oman and Pur Bahadur Gurung from Nepal.

On Friday, the Alpine Club of Pakistan said several climbers had been spotted by drones but their condition was unknown.

The club's secretary general, Ayaz Shigri, told the BBC rescuers were concerned about the risk of further avalanches.

The search and rescue operation for the team began after reports of an avalanche on Thursday on the 8,047-metre (26,400ft) peak in the Karakoram range.

The multinational climbing group was being led by Purja. He is known for climbing all 14 of the world's 8,000m-plus mountains in just over six months in 2019.

Purja joined the British Army in 2003 and the Special Boat Service - the special forces unit of the Royal Navy - in 2009.

In 2012, he reached the summit of the 6,119m Lobuche East mountain in Nepal - his first peak.

In June, Mallory Geis posted on social media that she was ready for "her first big kid climbing expedition in Pakistan".

Pur Bahadur Gurung - also known as Yukta - was certified by the International Federation of Mountain Guides Associations and close to completing the 14-peaks challenge.

Also among the group is Kili Pemba Sherpa Kili, who has so far scaled Everest 15 times. In 2021, he was a member of a historic K2 winter expedition, along with several Nepali climbers including Purja.

Broad Peak is regarded as one of the more challenging mountains for climbers. The first successful ascent was in 1957, when an Austrian expedition reached the summit.

Since then, many more have climbed the mountain, but dozens have lost their lives.

One of Broad Peak's deadliest years was 2013, when at least six fatalities were recorded.

Correction 31/7/26: A previous version of this story stated that four members of the expedition had been found dead, citing the Alpine Club of Pakistan. This was a miscommunication on its part and has since been amended.
body.zh: 当地政府机构称，世界最高山峰之一发生雪崩后，救援人员发现了美国登山者马洛里·盖斯的遗体。 星期四发生雪崩时，盖斯正在与中国接壤的巴基斯坦布洛阿特峰参加一个由 10 人组成的探险队。 另外两具尸体——来自阿曼的纳迪拉·艾哈迈德·阿卜杜拉·哈蒂和来自尼泊尔的普尔·巴哈杜尔·古伦——也已被确认。 据当地吉尔吉特·巴尔蒂斯坦信息部称，所有人都已被直升机送往医院，办理“身份识别法律手续”。 巴基斯坦阿尔卑斯山俱乐部最初表示，在巴基斯坦布洛阿特峰发现了四具尸体，随后澄清他们实际上发现了两具尸体和一个身体部位。 报告称，无人机还发现了另外几人，但他们的情况要等到周六救援工作恢复以及搜索小组到达该地区（这可能需要几个小时）后才能明朗。恶劣的天气一直困扰着他们。 巴基斯坦阿尔卑斯俱乐部补充说，一名登山者的下落仍然不明。 周四，喀喇昆仑山脉海拔 8,047 米（26,400 英尺）的山峰发生雪崩后，该团队开始了搜救行动。 巴基斯坦高山俱乐部表示，这支跨国登山队由出生于尼泊尔的著名登山家尼尔马尔·普贾 (Nirmal Purja) 领导。 他因在 2019 年仅用了六个月多的时间就攀登了世界上所有 14 座 8000 米以上的山峰而闻名。 巴基斯坦阿尔卑斯俱乐部告诉英国广播公司，它已经看到包括普贾在内的三名探险队成员的 GPS 追踪器的移动，但直升飞机在这些地点看不到任何东西。 救援人员后来发现其中一个追踪器被砸碎，这让他们相信他们所看到的运动可能是一个小故障。 巴基斯坦阿尔卑斯山俱乐部通讯负责人奈拉·基亚尼表示，超过24小时后，在如此恶劣的条件下生存的机会“非常渺茫”，但他补充说，“奇迹确实会发生”。 周五早些时候，高山俱乐部证实，巴基斯坦军队已派出两架救援直升机，搭载救援人员和其他专业设备来支持救援行动。 声明称：“俱乐部为所有登山者的安全和成功营救祈祷，并在这个困难时期与他们的家人和国际登山界站在一起。” Purja 于 2003 年加入英国陆军，并于 2009 年加入特种艇服务队（皇家海军特种部队）。 2012年，他去了珠穆朗玛峰大本营，没有返回加德满都，而是登顶了尼泊尔海拔6,119m的罗布其东山——他的第一座山峰。 与普贾一起攀登的是美国人马洛里·盖斯 (American Mallory Geis)。六月中旬，她...

reflection.en: The recovery of these climbers' bodies brings a somber reality to the dangers of the mountains and the fragility of life. In moments of profound loss and uncertainty, we remember that even Yahweh Himself grieved, showing us that sorrow is a natural and human response to death.
reflection.zh: 寻回这些登山者的遗体，沉重地提醒我们高山的危险和生命的脆弱。在深切的失落和不确定中，我们记得雅伟自己也曾哀哭，这表明悲伤是面对死亡时自然而人性的反应。

verse.textEn: Jesus wept.
verse.textZh: 耶稣哭了。

title.en: Russian strikes on Kyiv kill at least nine, Ukraine officials say
title.zh: 乌克兰官员称俄罗斯袭击基辅造成至少九人死亡

summary.en: Ukrainian officials report that at least nine people were killed in Russian strikes on Kyiv, as Moscow intensifies its ballistic missile attacks on the capital.
summary.zh: 乌克兰官员称，俄罗斯对基辅的袭击造成至少九人死亡，莫斯科正在加大对乌克兰首都的弹道导弹袭击力度。

body.en:
At least nine people have been killed in Russian ballistic missile strikes on Kyiv, local officials said.

A further 28 people were injured in the attack on the Ukrainian capital on Saturday morning, according to the country's State Emergency Service.

Moscow has escalated deadly ballistic missile attacks on Kyiv recently, prompting Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky to say that missile interceptors are urgently needed.

The strikes come two days after a suspected Russian cruise missile landed in Poland during a widespread attack on Ukraine that killed at least eight people, including six members of one family .

Kyiv's Mayor Vitali Klitschko said the capital had come under a ballistic missile attack on Saturday, with AFP reporting more than 10 explosions.

Klitschko said a residential building in Shevchenkivskyi was partially destroyed, trapping people inside.

The emergency services said at least seven people were killed in a strike in the Darnytskyi district. Another 14 were injured, including two children, it reported.

In Solomyanskyi district, two people died and eight were injured, including two children, as a five-storey residential building was partially destroyed, officials said.

The attack comes after Zelensky met President Donald Trump in Washington DC earlier this week to urge the US to grant Ukraine a licence to produce Patriot interceptor missiles.

Asked about the missiles during a cabinet meeting at the Camp David retreat on Friday, Trump said the US had not agreed to Ukraine building Patriot missiles but that talks were ongoing.

Emphasising concerns about sharing advanced US weaponry, Trump called it "a big step".

Trump's latest comments regarding Patriot missiles come weeks after he offered to give Ukraine the right to produce them.

As Russia has stepped up its air attacks, Ukraine has run low on supplies of Patriots, which remain the only weapon in its arsenal capable of downing ballistic missiles.

"I don't think this would ever happen, but, you know, those people that you give that technology, they can someday turn on you," Trump said.

Zelensky said in a post on X on Friday that he had followed up on his meeting with Trump with a "good" phone call with US Vice-President JD Vance.

"As Russia's air attacks on our country continue unabated, air defence – specifically Patriot interceptors against ballistic missiles – remains a top priority," Zelensky wrote.

For its part, Ukraine has escalated its retaliatory strikes in recent months, including attacks on several retail warehouses belonging to Russia's biggest online retailer, Wildberries.

Kyiv says it is targeting logistics hubs used by Russians to buy military equipment, and disrupting supplies to the Russian army.
body.zh: 当地官员称，俄罗斯对基辅的弹道导弹袭击已造成至少九人死亡。 据乌克兰国家紧急服务部门称，周六上午，乌克兰首都发生袭击，另有 28 人受伤。 莫斯科最近升级了对基辅的致命弹道导弹袭击，促使乌克兰总统泽连斯基表示迫切需要导弹拦截器。 两天前，一枚疑似俄罗斯巡航导弹在对乌克兰的大规模袭击中落在波兰，造成至少八人死亡，其中包括一个家庭的六名成员。 基辅市长维塔利·克里琴科表示，首都周六遭到弹道导弹袭击，法新社报道称发生了十多起爆炸。 克里琴科说，舍甫琴基夫斯基的一栋住宅楼部分被毁，有人被困在里面。 紧急服务部门表示，达尔尼茨基地区的一次罢工至少造成七人死亡。据报道，另有 14 人受伤，其中包括两名儿童。 官员称，索洛米扬斯基区一栋五层住宅楼部分被毁，造成两人死亡、八人受伤，其中包括两名儿童。 此次袭击发生之前，泽伦斯基本周早些时候在华盛顿特区会见了唐纳德·特朗普总统，敦促美国授予乌克兰生产爱国者拦截导弹的许可证。 周五在戴维营休养地举行的内阁会议上被问及导弹问题时，特朗普表示，美国尚未同意乌克兰制造爱国者导弹，但谈判仍在进行中。 特朗普强调了对共享美国先进武器的担忧，称这是“一大步”。 特朗普关于爱国者导弹的最新评论是在他提出给予乌克兰生产爱国者导弹的权利几周后发表的。 随着俄罗斯加强空袭，乌克兰的爱国者导弹供应不足，而爱国者导弹仍然是其武器库中唯一能够击落弹道导弹的武器。 特朗普说：“我认为这种情况永远不会发生，但是，你知道，那些你提供这项技术的人，有一天他们可能会背叛你。” 泽连斯基周五在 X 上发帖称，在与特朗普会面后，他与美国副总统 JD 万斯进行了“良好”的通话。 泽伦斯基写道：“随着俄罗斯对我国的空袭有增无减，防空——特别是针对弹道导弹的爱国者拦截器——仍然是重中之重。” 就乌克兰而言，近几个月来升级了报复性打击，其中包括对俄罗斯最大在线零售商 Wildberry 旗下的几个零售仓库的袭击。 基辅表示，它的目标是俄罗斯人用来购买军事装备的物流中心，并中断对俄罗斯军队的供应。

reflection.en: In the face of escalating violence and tragic loss of life, our hearts ache for those who mourn. This verse offers a profound hope that one day, Yahweh will bring an end to all suffering, wiping away every tear and abolishing death itself. It reminds us that even amidst the deepest pain, there is a promise of ultimate peace and restoration.
reflection.zh: 面对不断升级的暴力和悲惨的生命损失，我们的心为那些哀悼的人而痛。这节经文提供了一个深刻的盼望，即有一天，雅伟将终结所有的苦难，擦去每一滴眼泪，并废除死亡本身。它提醒我们，即使在最深的痛苦中，也有一个终极和平与复兴的应许。

verse.textEn: He will wipe every tear from their eyes. There will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain.
verse.textZh: 神要擦去他们一切的眼泪；不再有死亡，也不再有悲哀、哭号、疼痛。

title.en: ‘MPs have had their stomachs pumped’: concerns over ‘alcohol-soaked’ culture in Westminster
title.zh: “议员们曾被洗胃”：对威斯敏斯特“酒精浸泡”文化的担忧

summary.en: A report has revealed concerns about an “alcohol-soaked” culture in Westminster, describing Parliament as “Britain’s last alcohol-soaked workplace” where Members of Parliament are offered free drinks from midday, despite previous alcohol-related scandals and instances of MPs requiring medical attention.
summary.zh: 一份报告揭示了对威斯敏斯特“酒精浸泡”文化的担忧，称议会是“英国最后一个酒精浸泡的工作场所”，议员们从中午就开始获得免费酒水，尽管此前曾发生过与酒精相关的丑闻，甚至有议员需要洗胃。

body.en: Alcohol is embedded in profession where long hours, loneliness and lobbying are the norm, report finds Parliament is “Britain’s last alcohol-soaked workplace” where MPs are offered free drinks as early as midday despite alcohol-related scandals, a report has reveal ed. Drinking is commonplace and some MPs have had their stomachs pumped after consuming so much alcohol that they ended up in hospital, one disclosed. Continue reading...
body.zh: 报告发现，议会是“英国最后一个酒精浸透的工作场所”，尽管存在与酒精有关的丑闻，但国会议员早在中午就可以免费享用饮料。一名议员透露，饮酒是司空见惯的事，一些议员在喝了太多酒后被洗胃，最终入院治疗。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The report on Westminster's “alcohol-soaked” culture highlights the personal and professional challenges faced when habits compromise integrity and well-being. For those in public service, maintaining self-control is vital, recognizing that our bodies are a sacred trust. This calls for a culture that supports healthy choices, honoring both individual...
reflection.zh: 关于威斯敏斯特“酒精浸泡”文化的报告，凸显了当习惯损害诚信和福祉时，个人和职业所面临的挑战。对于从事公共服务的人来说，保持自制至关重要，要认识到我们的身体是神圣的托付。这呼吁建立一种支持健康选择的文化，既尊重个人尊严，也尊重公共责任。

verse.textEn: Do you not know that your bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit, who is in you, whom you have received from God? You are not your own.
verse.textZh: 岂不知你们的身子就是圣灵的殿吗？这圣灵是从神而来，住在你们里面的。并且你们不是自己的人。

title.en: EU relations, climate crisis and Gaza: why Ed Miliband is fired up by Foreign Office challenges
title.zh: 欧盟关系、气候危机和加沙：埃德·米利班德为何对外交部挑战充满热情

summary.en: Labour veteran Ed Miliband is reportedly enthusiastic about the challenges of the Foreign Office role, which involves navigating complex international relations, including negotiations with figures like Trump, upcoming G20 leadership, EU relations, the climate crisis, and the situation in Gaza.
summary.zh: 据报道，工党资深人士埃德·米利班德对外交大臣一职的挑战充满热情，该职位涉及处理复杂的国际关系，包括与特朗普等人物的谈判、即将到来的G20领导层、欧盟关系、气候危机以及加沙局势。

body.en: Labour veteran is said to relish role that requires careful negotiation of Trump and impending G20 leadership Extraordinarily, given the importance of geopolitics, the office of foreign secretary has sometimes appeared a consolation prize in British politics, perhaps reflecting the transfer of responsibility to Downing Street or the Cabinet Office. That is not how Ed Miliband views the job. His allies say suggestions that he nurses resentment after he was deprived of the chance to be chancellor misunderstand his grasp of the policy challenges ahead. “Ed has an immense appetite to get things done and is relishing being in this job,” one says. “Ed will be a policy-driven foreign secretary.” Continue reading...
body.zh: 据说，工党退伍军人喜欢扮演需要与特朗普进行仔细谈判和即将到来的G20领导层的角色。不同寻常的是，考虑到地缘政治的重要性，外交大臣办公室有时在英国政治中似乎是一个安慰奖，这或许反映出责任已转移到唐宁街或内阁办公室。埃德·米利班德并不是这样看待这份工作的。他的盟友表示，有关他被剥夺担任总理机会后怀有怨恨的说法误解了他对未来政策挑战的把握。一位人士表示：“艾德对完成工作有着极大的兴趣，并且很享受这份工作。” “埃德将成为一位政策驱动的外交大臣。”继续阅读...

reflection.en: The demanding role of foreign secretary, navigating complex global issues and difficult relationships, highlights the constant human endeavor to foster peace. Yahweh's word encourages us to pursue peace with all people, as far as it depends on us, even amidst significant international challenges. This pursuit requires wisdom, patience, and a commitment to...
reflection.zh: 外交大臣这一要求严苛的职位，需要处理复杂的全球问题和艰难的关系，这凸显了人类为促进和平所做的持续努力。雅伟的话语鼓励我们，只要力所能及，就要与所有人和平相处，即使面对重大的国际挑战。这种追求在一个分裂的世界中需要智慧、耐心和对话的承诺。

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
verse.textZh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

title.en: First Australian mass mortality event suspected as deadly bird flu virus rapidly escalates among native birds
title.zh: 澳大利亚首次大规模死亡事件疑因致命禽流感病毒在本地鸟类中迅速升级

summary.en: Helicopter surveillance has revealed over 80 dead and sick greater crested terns off the South Australian coast, suspected to be the first mass mortality event in Australia caused by the rapidly spreading H5 bird flu virus among native birds.
summary.zh: 直升机监测发现南澳大利亚海岸有80多只凤头燕鸥死亡或生病，这被怀疑是澳大利亚首次由迅速蔓延的H5禽流感病毒导致的原生鸟类大规模死亡事件。

body.en: Helicopter surveillance finds dead and dying greater crested terns off South Australian coast as H5 virus spreads Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast More than 80 dead and sick birds seen on rocks off the South Australian coast are suspected to be the first mass mortality event from the deadly H5N1 bird flu virus, only six weeks after the disease arrived in Australia. reflection.en: The news of a mass mortality event among native birds reminds us of the fragility of creation and the widespread impact of disease on ecosystems. Yahweh's Word tells us that the whole creation groans under the weight of brokenness, longing for renewal. This tragedy calls us to lament the suffering in the natural world and to seek ways to care for the earth...
reflection.zh: 原生鸟类大规模死亡事件的消息提醒我们，受造界是脆弱的，疾病对生态系统有着广泛的影响。雅伟的话语告诉我们，整个受造界都在破碎的重压下呻吟，渴望更新。这场悲剧呼唤我们为自然界的苦难哀叹，并寻求方法来照管雅伟托付给我们的地球。

verse.textEn: We know that the whole creation has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth right up to the present time.
verse.textZh: 我们知道，一切受造之物一同叹息、劳苦，直到如今。

title.en: ‘A symbol of resistance’: the fight to save treehouse built on no man’s land next to Berlin Wall
title.zh: “抵抗的象征”：为拯救柏林墙旁无人区树屋而战

summary.en: A treehouse built on the former no man's land next to the Berlin Wall by a Turkish creator is now a focal point of a preservation effort. Supporters hope to save the structure, which they see as a symbol of resistance, from demolition due to safety concerns, advocating for its transformation into a memorial honoring...
summary.zh: 一棵由一位土耳其建造者在柏林墙旁的前无人区建造的树屋，正成为一项保护工作的焦点。支持者们希望将这个被他们视为抵抗象征的结构从因安全隐患而被拆除的命运中拯救出来，并倡导将其改造为纪念战后外国劳工的纪念碑。

body.en: Supporters fear structure could be torn down as safety hazard and want it to become memorial to postwar foreign labourers in honour of its Turkish creator Sometimes the currents of history converge in a single spot. In Berlin, one of the most intriguing of those places is a small traffic island with a lovingly tended garden and a ramshackle two-storey structure called the Treehouse at the Wall. In 1983, Osman Kalin, a Turkish “ guest worker ”, was looking in his corner of the city cleaved by the Berlin Wall for a patch of earth in which to plant his onions, garlic and cucumbers. Virtually on his doorstep in the Kreuzberg district was a slice of no man’s land next to the concrete barrier and barbed wire. Although it sat in West Berlin, cold war logic meant the lot officially belonged to the communist East. Continue reading...

title.en: Fifa scraps controversial World Cup investment plan
title.zh: 国际足联取消备受争议的世界杯投资计划

summary.en: Football's world governing body Fifa abandons plans to sell off stakes in its major competitions after widespread opposition to president Gianni Infantino's proposal.
summary.zh: 国际足球管理机构国际足联（FIFA）在主席詹尼·因凡蒂诺的提议遭到广泛反对后，放弃了出售其主要赛事股份的计划。

body.en:
Fifa president Gianni Infantino says he has scrapped the controversial plan to sell off stakes in the governing body's competitions to private investors following widespread opposition.

Infantino said it had become clear the project had "created divisions" that are "no longer in the interest" of its original objective.

Infantino had offered Fifa's 211 member associations $40m (£30m) if they backed a proposal for private investment in its tournaments, including the men's and women's World Cups.

However, Uefa - which governs European football - responded by voting to boycott World Cups if the plans went ahead, and other governing bodies also voiced their opposition.

On Friday, Fifa's chief operating officer Kevin Lamour said the governing body's own administration had been "deceived" about the project.

Carlos Cordeiro - Infantino's senior adviser on global strategy and governance - resigned over the matter, saying the proposal was "a bad deal for football" and would "mortgage football's future".

Concacaf, which governs football in North, Central America and the Caribbean - and hosted this summer's World Cup - said its members "rejected" the proposal, with sources saying the vast majority of associations from the region are losing, or have lost, faith in Infantino.

The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) said it stood in "solidarity" with Uefa and Concacaf, while UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Infantino was "the wrong man" to lead Fifa.

It means Infantino is now under immense pressure as he seeks re-election for a fourth term as president at the Fifa Congress in March.

"Our purpose has always been - and will always be - to unite and improve," the 56-year-old added in a statement.

"Moving forward, my intent is to bring all interested parties back together in the coming days and weeks in the spirit of shared interest in our game."

AFC president Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim Al Khalifa welcomed the withdrawal of the plan.

"The future of global football must always be shaped through proper consultation, collective dialogue and respect for the established governance structures of our game," he said.

Despite rejections from Uefa and Concacaf, Fifa initially vowed to continue with its proposals on Friday, saying "nobody is selling football".

However, Infantino would have needed the backing of a majority of member associations to pass the plans - meaning 106 of its 211 members needed to vote in favour.

That became unlikely when the AFC joined Uefa and Concacaf in opposing the plans.

If all member associations backed the stance of their governing body, that would have meant 136 nations voting against Infantino's plan.

Governing bodies in Africa (CAF) and Oceania (OFC) had said they would discuss Fifa's plan in August.

body.zh: 国际足联主席詹尼·因凡蒂诺表示，由于受到广泛反对，他已经取消了向私人投资者出售国际足联赛事股份的有争议的计划。 因凡蒂诺表示，很明显该项目“造成了分裂”，“不再符合其最初目标的利益”。 因凡蒂诺向国际足联的 211 个会员协会提供了 4000 万美元（3000 万英镑）的资金，如果他们支持私人投资国际足联锦标赛（包括男子和女子世界杯）的提议。 然而，管理欧洲足球的欧足联做出回应，如果该计划继续下去，将投票抵制世界杯，其他管理机构也表示反对。 周五，国际足联首席运营官凯文·拉穆尔表示，管理机构自己的政府在该项目上受到了“欺骗”。 因凡蒂诺全球战略和治理高级顾问卡洛斯·科代罗因此事辞职，称该提议“对足球来说是一笔糟糕的交易”，并将“抵押足球的未来”。 管理北美、中美洲和加勒比地区足球并主办今年夏天世界杯的中北美及加勒比地区足球协会表示，其成员“拒绝”了这一提议，消息人士称，该地区绝大多数协会正在或已经失去对因凡蒂诺的信心。 亚洲足球联合会（AFC）表示与欧足联和中北美及加勒比地区足联“团结一致”，而英国首相安迪·伯纳姆则表示因凡蒂诺是领导国际足联的“错误人选”。 这意味着因凡蒂诺在三月份的国际足联代表大会上寻求连任第四任主席，现在面临着巨大的压力。 这位 56 岁的老人在一份声明中补充道：“我们的目标一直是，也将永远是，团结和进步。” “展望未来，我的目的是本着对我们游戏的共同兴趣的精神，在未来几天和几周内让所有感兴趣的各方重新聚集在一起。” 亚足联主席谢赫·萨勒曼·本·易卜拉欣·阿勒哈利法对撤回该计划表示欢迎。 “全球足球的未来必须始终通过适当的协商、集体对话和尊重我们足球运动的既定治理结构来塑造，”他说。 尽管遭到欧足联和中北美及加勒比地区足联的拒绝，国际足联最初在周五发誓要继续其提议，称“没有人出售足球”。 然而，因凡蒂诺需要大多数会员协会的支持才能通过该计划，这意味着其 211 名会员中需要有 106 名投票赞成。 当亚足联与欧足联和中北美及加勒比地区足联一起反对该计划后，这种情况变得不太可能发生。 如果所有成员协会都支持其管理机构的立场，那就意味着有 136 个国家投票反对因凡蒂诺的计划。 非洲（CAF）和大洋洲（OFC）的管理机构表示，他们将在八月份讨论国际足联的计划。 Conmebol——南美...

reflection.en: Even in complex global organizations, decisions benefit from diverse perspectives. The abandonment of a controversial plan after widespread opposition highlights the wisdom found when leaders heed collective counsel. This echoes the principle that safety often lies in the abundance of advisors.
reflection.zh: 即使在全球复杂的组织中，决策也受益于多元的视角。一项备受争议的计划在遭到广泛反对后被放弃，这突显了领导者听取集体意见时所能发现的智慧。这与“谋士众多，人便安居”的原则不谋而合。

verse.textZh: 无智谋，民就败落；谋士多，人便安居。

title.en: Israeli West Bank settler tells BBC attacks on Palestinians are justified as revenge
title.zh: 约旦河西岸定居者告诉BBC，袭击巴勒斯坦人是正当的复仇行为

summary.en: Settler violence against Palestinians is reportedly increasing in the West Bank, coinciding with the expansion of Israeli settlements and outposts in the region.
summary.zh: 据报道，随着以色列定居点和前哨的扩张，约旦河西岸针对巴勒斯坦人的定居者暴力事件正在增加。

body.en:
The Israeli settler outpost of Havat Gilad, deep inside the occupied West Bank, is spread across several hilltops, its sheds and simple block houses clearly visible from neighbouring Palestinian villages.

Last weekend saw a wave of settler attacks on Palestinian villages in the area, after an Israeli security guard from Havat Gilad was killed during a confrontation between Palestinians and Israelis in the village of Tal last Friday.

Four Palestinians and an Israeli soldier were also killed in the incident, the original cause of which is disputed.

After spending the weekend speaking to Palestinians around Havat Gilad , we drove into the outpost itself, to ask one of its residents about the violence, and the expansion of Israeli settlements in the West Bank.

It is rare for an international media organisation like the BBC to be allowed into these outposts. But on this occasion, Yehuda Shimon, a lawyer with an organisation that represents Israelis arrested for violence against Palestinians, agreed to speak.

He told me that attacks on Palestinian villages last weekend were justified as revenge for the killing of the outpost's security guard.

"I think now, after they killed one Israeli, we need to kill all the people in Tal and Sarra, even Jit and Farata," he said, naming the Palestinian villages closest to the outpost.

I put it to him that he was equating one Jewish life with hundreds or even thousands of Palestinian lives.

"Yes, I know," he replied. "But this is the truth, because God chose us [and] because of this you are jealous."

These extreme views – rejected by many Israelis – are crucial to understanding the conflict playing out across the West Bank, as Israel's settlements and outposts expand, and violence against Palestinians grows.

Many settlers here, especially in unauthorised outposts like Havat Gilad, built without Israeli planning permission or legal oversight, see the West Bank as land given to the Jewish people by God.

Both Israel's official settlements and its unauthorised outposts are illegal under international law.

Havat Gilad was established more than 20 years ago, in memory of an Israeli security officer murdered by Palestinians – a loosely scattered collection of houses with a vineyard perched high on one hill.

When we visit there is a row of newly burned buildings near the entrance – the result, Shimon says, of an arson attack by Palestinians. Israeli media reported that police were treating the fire as accidental, caused by cigarette butts thrown from a car window.

Israel's government has previously said it would legalise Havat Gilad. The Israeli organisation Peace Now, which monitors settlements, says it has been unable to do so because much of the land it is built on is recognised by Israel as privately owned by...
body.zh: 以色列定居者哈瓦特吉拉德前哨基地位于被占领的约旦河西岸深处，分布在几个山顶上，从邻近的巴勒斯坦村庄可以清楚地看到其棚屋和简单的街区房屋。 上周五，一名来自哈瓦特吉拉德的以色列保安在塔尔村巴勒斯坦人和以色列人的对抗中被杀，上周末，该地区的巴勒斯坦村庄遭到了定居者的一波袭击。 四名巴勒斯坦人和一名以色列士兵也在事件中丧生，事件的起因尚有争议。 在周末与哈瓦特吉拉德周围的巴勒斯坦人交谈后，我们驱车进入前哨基地，向一名居民询问暴力事件以及以色列在西岸定居点的扩张情况。 像英国广播公司这样的国际媒体机构被允许进入这些前哨基地是很少见的。但这一次，代表因暴力侵害巴勒斯坦人而被捕的以色列人的组织的律师耶胡达·西蒙(Yehuda Shimon)同意发言。 他告诉我，上周末对巴勒斯坦村庄的袭击是对前哨保安被杀的报复。 “我认为现在，在他们杀死一名以色列人之后，我们需要杀死塔尔和萨拉的所有人，甚至吉特和法拉塔，”他说，并提到了最靠近前哨基地的巴勒斯坦村庄。 我告诉他，他将一个犹太人的生命等同于数百甚至数千巴勒斯坦人的生命。 “是的，我知道，”他回答道。 “但这是事实，因为上帝选择了我们，因此你嫉妒。” 随着以色列定居点和前哨基地的扩张以及针对巴勒斯坦人的暴力行为的增加，这些被许多以色列人拒绝的极端观点对于理解整个西岸正在发生的冲突至关重要。 这里的许多定居者，特别是像哈瓦特吉拉德这样未经以色列规划许可或法律监督而建造的前哨基地，将西岸视为上帝赐予犹太人的土地。 根据国际法，以色列的官方定居点及其未经授权的前哨基地都是非法的。 哈瓦特吉拉德 (Havat Gilad) 建于 20 多年前，是为了纪念一名被巴勒斯坦人谋杀的以色列安全官员，这里是一组松散分散的房屋，葡萄园高高地坐落在一座小山上。 当我们参观时，入口附近有一排新近被烧毁的建筑——西蒙说，这是巴勒斯坦人纵火袭击的结果。以色列媒体报道称，警方将此次火灾视为意外，是由车窗扔出的烟头引起的。 以色列政府此前曾表示将使哈瓦特吉拉德合法化。监测定居点的以色列组织“立即和平”表示，它一直无法这样做，因为它所建的大部分土地都被以色列承认为私人拥有……

reflection.en: The justification of violence as revenge risks perpetuating a cycle where harm begets more harm, a pattern that history often confirms. Yahweh's word reminds us that those who live by the sword often face its consequences, urging us to seek paths that break this destructive cycle.
reflection.zh: 以复仇为名的暴力辩护，有使伤害循环往复的危险，这是一种历史常态。雅伟的话语提醒我们，凡动刀的，必死在刀下，敦促我们寻求打破这种破坏性循环的道路。

verse.textEn: All who draw the sword will die by the sword.
verse.textZh: 凡动刀的，必死在刀下。

title.en: Police renew appeal, release ransom notes six months after Nancy Guthrie vanished
title.zh: 警方在南希·格思里失踪六个月后再次呼吁，并公布勒索信

summary.en: Police have renewed their appeal for information and released ransom notes six months after 84-year-old Nancy Guthrie disappeared. Alleged kidnappers initially demanded millions in bitcoin before later claiming she had died.
summary.zh: 在南希·格思里（Nancy Guthrie）失踪六个月后，警方再次呼吁公众提供线索，并公布了勒索信。据称，绑架者最初索要数百万比特币，后来声称这位84岁的老人已经死亡。

body.en:
Two ransom notes purportedly written by kidnappers who abducted the mother of US "Today" show co-host Savannah Guthrie have been released, six months after Nancy Guthrie vanished in Arizona, as investigators renewed efforts to identify the culprits.

Copies of the two email messages were posted online by the Pima County Sheriff's Department with a notice appealing again to members of the public to come forward with information that might help identify the masked prowler caught on video by Nancy Guthrie's doorbell camera outside her home around the time she went missing.

Both notes, initially delivered to news outlets before being turned over to authorities, have been widely reported in the media, along with some details of their contents, since early in the investigation. But the full texts had not been previously disclosed.

The first, from 2 February — a day after the 84-year-old Guthrie was reported missing — demanded US $4 million ($5.7 million) to be paid in Bitcoin within three days, and warned that if the deadline were missed "the ransom will be increased to US $6 million" ($8.56 million) due by the following Monday.

"Your mother is aware of this and her life is in your hands," the note said, adding, "there will be no negotiation. Do not play games, law enforcement will not be able to help you."

The message also contained details meant to authenticate it, saying that Guthrie's wristwatch had been left on the floor at the foot of her bed, and a backyard floodlight was "destroyed".

The second note, received on 6 February and addressed to the "Guthrie Family," delivered more grim news.

"She perished shortly after she was taken. We believe it was heart-related. She is buried in nature now."

It concludes: "We want your family to know this and hope you all can find peace. We are truly sorry."

In the latest of several videos posted to social media since her mother was taken, Savannah Guthrie, longtime co-anchor of the flagship NBC morning news program, appealed to the kidnappers on Monday to "do the right thing" and "tell us where to look for her".

Nancy Guthrie, in frail health with limited mobility, was last seen alive on 31 January at her home in Tucson. She was reported missing on 1 February after a friend alerted family that she did not appear for Sunday church services as expected.

title.en: FIFA abandons World Cup privatisation plan after fierce backlash
title.zh: 国际足联在强烈反对后放弃世界杯私有化计划

summary.en: FIFA has withdrawn its proposal to sell a 20 per cent stake in the World Cup to private investors, following significant public opposition. The plan involved creating a commercial subsidiary for the global football tournament.
summary.zh: 国际足联（FIFA）在遭到强烈反对后，放弃了将世界杯私有化的计划。此前，国际足联曾提议成立一家商业子公司，向私人投资者出售世界杯20%的股份。

body.en:
FIFA has abandoned plans to sell a stake in the World Cup after fierce backlash, including threats of boycotts.

In a statement on Saturday morning, FIFA president Gianni Infantino said it had "become clear that the project has created divisions of a nature that, regardless of the level of support, are no longer in the interest of the objective set out in the first place".

"Our purpose has always been — and will always be — to unite and improve," he said.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"Moving forward, my intent is to bring all interested parties back together in the coming days and weeks in the spirit of shared interest in our game, and with the objective to continue growing football everywhere, particularly in those countries that mostly need our support."

FIFA on Wednesday announced its plan to create a commercial subsidiary known as the FIFA Forward Enterprise that would run its main events, including the World Cup.

Private investors would have been able to buy a minority stake of up to 20 per cent in the subsidiary, which was valued up to US$20 billion ($28.47 billion).

FIFA had promised each of its 211 member countries and territories US$40 million ($56.9 million) in funding for the 2027-2030 cycle if they agreed to the plan.

But the backlash to the proposal was fierce, with the 55 member states of the European football governing body UEFA voting unanimously to boycott all FIFA tournaments.

Other bodies also opposed the plan, including CONCACAF, the regional federation for North America, Central America and the Caribbean, as did the Asian Football Confederation, of which Australia is a part of.

Infantino's senior adviser Carlos Cordeiro resigned and called the plan a "bad deal for football", while FIFA chief operating officer Kevin Lamour said staff had been "deceived" by Infantino and the proposal was a "project of one person".

This reminds us that pursuing wealth can often conflict with deeper values and communal good, making it difficult to serve both Mammon and the broader community.

title.en: At least 57 migrants die crossing into Spanish enclave, as thousands voluntarily return
title.zh: 至少57名移民在进入西班牙飞地时死亡，数千人自愿返回

summary.en: At least 57 migrants died while attempting to cross into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta. The Spanish government reported that the majority of the over 50,000 migrants who had entered the territory have since returned to Morocco.
summary.zh: 至少有57名移民在试图进入西班牙飞地休达时死亡。西班牙政府表示，此前进入该地区的5万多名移民中，绝大多数已返回摩洛哥。

body.en:
The Spanish government says it has reversed a huge rush of migrants into a Spanish enclave in north Africa, with most of the more than 50,000 people who had crossed the border by land and sea already heading back voluntarily.

The Spanish government's representative in Ceuta said 57 bodies had been recovered on the Spanish side of the border and that there could be additional casualties on the Moroccan side. It said some drowned and some were crushed while trying to climb the breakwater that holds the border fence.

Spain's interior ministry said around 50,000 people had crossed the border since Thursday morning, and estimated that 48,300 had returned by 6 pm on Friday (2am Saturday AEST). Juan Jesus Vivas, head of Ceuta's local government, said as many as 60,000 people had pushed across over the past couple of days.

Moroccan forces beat back crowds with batons and tear gas at the gates to Ceuta, trying to prevent more from entering the tiny Spanish territory that juts on a spit of sandy land into the Mediterranean from Morocco.

The rush on the border caused division in Europe, where leaders of fellow EU states called for Spain to ensure that the incident was contained.

Italy said it was suspending the European Union's border-free Schengen arrangements with Spain, a measure set to affect people travelling by plane or boat between the two countries. Madrid said the move violated EU treaties.

Reuters news agency reporters at the enclave's border saw Moroccan police in riot gear using tear gas to disperse some of the people amassed near the fences. Water cannon trucks were deployed and the charred remains of a bus and seven cars could be seen from clashes with the crowds.

On the other side, Spanish military vehicles lined up along sections of the border as dozens of migrants watched from a hilltop in Morocco, unable to cross.

Several hundred people could be seen returning to Morocco through border posts and holes in the fence, with some saying they could not find food or shelter in Ceuta.

"Honestly, I don't even know why I came, and now I'm going back," a young Moroccan man, who said he was from Tangier, told Reuters.

"I haven't eaten since lunch yesterday, even though I brought some money with me ... What we're doing is neither good nor enjoyable."

Ayman, a 20-year-old hairdresser from the port city of Larache who only gave one name, told Reuters he had crossed on Wednesday after a five-hour swim.

"There was no food inside Ceuta and we were kicked out badly by the [Spanish] army," he said.

title.en: The controversial detail Aussie viewers may have missed in Nolan's The Odyssey

summary.en: A specific detail reportedly omitted from Christopher Nolan's film "The Odyssey" has drawn criticism from some viewers and sparked public discussion.
summary.zh: 据报道，克里斯托弗·诺兰的电影《奥德赛》中一个特定细节的缺失引发了一些观众的批评和公众讨论。

body.en:
Christopher Nolan has brought one of the oldest surviving works of literature to the silver screen. But there's something missing in his blockbuster adaptation of The Odyssey — Greeks.

The director's revitalisation of the ancient Greek epic poem has no leading cast member of Greek ancestry. It's a choice that's drawn extensive criticism, particularly from Greek audiences.

"I'm not arguing that every character needed to be played by a Greek actor, and I'm not objecting to its diverse casting," one social media user said.

"I'm saying that in this enormous international cast, it would have been wonderful to see one Greek actor, maybe an unknown actor in a breakout role," said another.

"I'm gonna go see this movie, and I'm gonna try my best to enjoy it," another said.

"But I know that the whole time there's gonna be my Greek side and my American side watching at the same time and it's gonna be real tough to keep the Greek side quiet."

A third questioned whether "a single other culture" would be comfortable with a portrayal that lacks "a single actor, cultural adviser, academic, or director involved from that culture".

The film has made headlines for its star-studded cast, with US actor Matt Damon leading as Odysseus — Trojan War veteran and king of Ithaca.

The film follows Odysseus' role in the Trojan War and his decade-long journey home, where he reunites with his wife, Penelope, played by Anne Hathaway, and son Telemachus, played by Tom Holland.

Robert Pattinson, Charlize Theron, Lupita Nyong'o, Travis Scott, Elliot Page, Zendaya, John Leguizamo and Benny Safdie are among those cast in the feature.

Discourse has surrounded the casting since it was announced in 2024. Some have praised Nolan's racially diverse cast, while others have questioned his intentions.

Vrasidas Karalis, professor of modern Greek and Byzantine studies at the University of Sydney, said the original epic — widely attributed to ancient Greek poet Homer — was created at a time when the Mediterranean was multicultural, so the expectation that the cast would be exclusively Greek isn't true to the text.

"The story itself is so complex and involves so many different people. During the wanderings of Odysseus, he meets all these different people, the lotus-eaters, the cyclops, the cannibals, all of these different sorts of tribes around the Mediterranean back then," he said.

"Asking to have Greeks there is a bit of a long shot, I would say. It's very multinational, multicultural and multi-religious."

He said the criticism from the Greek community is "parochial" and shows "a social and moral panic".

title.en: Sudan civil war: When drones strike the classroom
title.zh: 苏丹内战：当无人机袭击教室时

summary.en: Children in el-Obeid, Sudan, are living in fear and unable to attend school due to ongoing drone attacks targeting civilian areas. Aid organizations are highlighting the escalating humanitarian crisis in the besieged city.
summary.zh: 苏丹被围困城市奥贝德的儿童因无人机袭击民用基础设施而不敢上学。援助组织警告称，人道主义危机正在恶化。

body.en:
Children in Sudan's besieged city of el-Obeid are afraid to go to school as drone attacks hit civilian infrastructure. Aid groups warn of a worsening humanitarian crisis.

Flattened houses and rubble where a school once stood: These are the scenes that have appeared in footage of the Sudanese city of el-Obeid  published by Ayin Network, a nonpartisan Sudanese media outlet.

Drone attacks by the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) have caused enormous damage to civilian infrastructure, including power grids, transformers, water treatment plants, schools, universities and hospitals in the capital of North Kordofan.

The local population is struggling to survive, according to Ahmed Awad, a native of el-Obeid and a project manager for children's rights organization Plan International there. The city — whose population previously numbered half a million but has now become home to several hundred thousand people who are displaced — is under siege, he added.

There is a shortage of medical supplies as well as food and safe, clean water, and Awad said he saw long lines of people at just one water pump: "Sometimes you can spend all day to get one liter of water for two or three days." Most of the time, children and teenagers are the ones sent to fetch water.

He added that a drone had hit a primary school and killed three children, which had caused trauma among other children, many of whom no longer dared go to school.

"One of the mothers said three of her children cannot sleep because they are always in fear of something happening again," he said.

Even when they're sitting in their classrooms, they live with the constant fear that a drone could strike at any moment. Awad and his colleagues at Plan International are working to provide psychological support to the affected children. 

El-Obeid is a strategically important location. The city is a trading hub in the middle of the desert on the only major route between Sudan's capital, Khartoum — which is controlled by the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) — and the western Darfur region, large parts of which are under the control of the RSF. 

El-Obeid is currently controlled by the army, which has some 13,000 soldiers stationed there, and has been on the front line since fighting shifted from Darfur to Kordofan at the beginning of the year. The RSF has deployed troops to about 30 kilometers (18.6 miles) beyond the city limits, and has been using drones to bomb civilian infrastructure.

Analysts, aid organizations and the United Nations have warned that the RSF could soon capture el-Obeid. They fear a similar scenario to that which unfolded in the city of el-Fasher in the neighboring...
body.zh: 由于无人机袭击袭击了民用基础设施，苏丹被围困城市奥贝德的儿童不敢上学。援助组织警告人道主义危机正在恶化。 曾经有一所学校矗立的房屋和瓦砾被夷为平地：这些场景出现在苏丹无党派媒体 Ayin Network 发布的苏丹奥贝德市的镜头中。 准军事快速支援部队（RSF）的无人机袭击对北科尔多凡州首府的民用基础设施造成了巨大破坏，包括电网、变压器、水处理厂、学校、大学和医院。 艾哈迈德·阿瓦德是奥贝德人，也是当地儿童权利组织国际计划的项目经理，他表示，当地居民正在为生存而苦苦挣扎。他补充说，这座城市以前的人口有 50 万，但现在已经成为数十万人流离失所的家园。 医疗用品、食品和安全清洁的水都短缺，阿瓦德说，他看到人们在一个水泵前排起长队：“有时你需要花一整天的时间才能获得两三天的一升水。” 大多数时候，孩子和青少年是被派去取水的。 他补充说，一架无人机袭击了一所小学并杀死了三名儿童，这给其他儿童造成了创伤，其中许多人不再敢去上学。 “一位母亲说，她的三个孩子无法入睡，因为他们总是担心再次发生什么事情，”他说。 即使当他们坐在教室里时，他们也一直担心无人机随时可能袭击。 阿瓦德和他在国际计划的同事正在努力为受影响的儿童提供心理支持。 埃尔奥贝德是一个具有重要战略意义的地点。 这座城市是沙漠中部的一个贸易中心，位于苏丹首都喀土穆（由苏丹武装部队 (SAF) 控制）和西达尔富尔地区（其中大部分地区由无国界部队控制）之间的唯一主要路线上。 埃尔-奥贝德目前由军队控制，军队驻扎着约 13,000 名士兵，自今年年初战事从达尔富尔转移到科尔多凡以来，埃尔奥贝德一直处于前线。无国界医生组织已将部队部署到城市边界外约 30 公里（18.6 英里）处，并一直在使用无人机轰炸民用基础设施。 分析人士、援助组织和联合国警告说，无国界医生组织可能很快就会抓获奥贝德。他们担心会发生与邻近的法希尔市类似的情况……

reflection.en: The targeting of schools and civilian areas in conflict zones inflicts profound trauma, especially on children who deserve safety and peace. Yahweh's word warns of severe consequences for those who cause harm to the innocent, reminding us of the sacred duty to protect the most vulnerable among us. May we pray for an end to such violence and for the...
reflection.zh: 冲突地区针对学校和民用设施的袭击给儿童带来了深重创伤，他们理应享有安全与和平。雅伟的话语警告，那些伤害无辜者的人将面临严厉后果，提醒我们保护最脆弱群体的神圣职责。愿我们为结束此类暴力，并为每一个身陷其中的儿童得到保护而祷告。

verse.textEn: If anyone causes one of these little ones — those who believe in me — to stumble, it would be better for them to have a large millstone hung around their neck and to be drowned in the depths of the sea.
verse.textZh: 凡使这信我的一个小子跌倒的，倒不如把大磨石拴在这人的颈项上，沉在深海里。
verse.themeEn: Woe to those who harm children

title.en: Humanoid robots: Trump's latest China trade battle?
title.zh: 人形机器人：特朗普最新的对华贸易战？

summary.en: The US has banned foreign-made humanoid robots, a market Chinese tech firms dominate. Although Washington cited national security risks, analysts think Donald Trump is buying time for US robot makers to catch up.
summary.zh: 美国已禁止外国制造的人形机器人，而中国科技公司在该市场占据主导地位。尽管华盛顿引用国家安全风险为由，但分析人士认为唐纳德·特朗普此举是为了给美国机器人制造商争取追赶的时间。

body.en:
The US has banned foreign-made humanoid robots, a market Chinese tech firms dominates. Although Washington cited national security risks, analysts think Donald Trump is buying time for US robot makers to catch up.

In the latest sign of China's threat to the United States's tech dominance, the Trump administration on Tuesday banned new foreign-made humanoid and four-legged robots from entering the country.

The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) cited "unacceptable risks" to national security for the decision.

The FCC noted how the robots "collect data that could be leveraged by malign actors to surveil Americans, enhance the capabilities of foreign intelligence services, or to remotely commandeer the robots."

The move is widely seen as aimed squarely at China, which accounted for 85% of humanoid robot deployments last year, according to British bank Barclays.

US officials warn that Chinese humanoid and quadruped (four-legged) robots can collect detailed location and personal data, be controlled remotely and pose risks for critical US infrastructure. Specific concerns center on the robots' potential dual-use — civilian and military purposes.

Unitree Robotics, a leading Chinese robot maker, appears on the Pentagon's list of firms with links to the Chinese military. Its robots have been used in army exercises.

Researchers have also shown that Unitree robots have security flaws that let attackers take control with a voice command and then use one robot to control others.

Washington is also concerned that a large cohort of low-cost Chinese robots could feed real-world data back to Chinese artificial intelligence (AI) systems, which are fast catching up with their US rivals.

The threat, however, is largely theoretical as most commercial humanoid robots are in early stages of development.

China has rejected the accusations, insisting the US is using national security as a pretext for protectionism to suppress Chinese technology . Beijing is expected to impose countermeasures, which could include curbs on the raw materials US robotics firms urgently need to scale up production.

The Trump administration has made no secret of its desire to help the domestic US robotics industry, which in turn supports the country's nearly trillion-dollar AI buildout. According to industry watchers, US President Donald Trump wants to ensure the likes of Figure AI, Tesla Optimus and Agility Robotics are protected from high-volume Chinese producers, whose robots often cost half the price or less of their US rivals.

Washington has put similar curbs on Chinese drones and solar panels and now levies a 100% tariff on Chinese electric vehicles .

The ban is widely seen as Trump's attempt to buy time, having been caught off guard by how...
body.zh: 美国已禁止外国制造的人形机器人，而中国科技公司在这个市场上占据主导地位。尽管华盛顿提到了国家安全风险，但分析人士认为唐纳德·特朗普正在为美国机器人制造商迎头赶上争取时间。 中国威胁美国科技主导地位的最新迹象是，特朗普政府周二禁止新型外国制造的人形机器人和四足机器人进入该国。 美国联邦通信委员会 (FCC) 称这一决定对国家安全存在“不可接受的风险”。 美国联邦通信委员会指出，这些机器人如何“收集可能被恶意行为者利用的数据来监视美国人、增强外国情报部门的能力或远程征用机器人。” 人们普遍认为此举直接针对中国，据英国巴克莱银行称，去年中国的仿人机器人部署量占到了 85%。 美国官员警告说，中国的人形机器人和四足机器人可以收集详细的位置和个人数据，进行远程控制，并对美国关键基础设施构成风险。具体关注点集中在机器人潜在的双重用途——民用和军事用途。 中国领先的机器人制造商优树机器人公司出现在五角大楼与中国军方有联系的公司名单上。其机器人已用于军队演习。 研究人员还表明，Unitree 机器人存在安全缺陷，攻击者可以通过语音命令进行控制，然后使用一个机器人来控制其他机器人。 华盛顿还担心大量低成本的中国机器人可能会将真实世界的数据反馈给中国人工智能（AI）系统，而中国人工智能系统正在迅速赶上美国竞争对手。 然而，这种威胁很大程度上只是理论上的，因为大多数商业人形机器人还处于开发的早期阶段。 中国否认了这些指控，坚称美国正在利用国家安全作为保护主义的借口来打压中国技术。预计北京将采取反制措施，其中可能包括限制美国机器人公司扩大生产规模急需的原材料。 特朗普政府毫不掩饰其帮助美国国内机器人行业的愿望，这反过来又支持了该国近万亿美元的人工智能建设。据行业观察人士称，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普希望确保Figure AI、特斯拉 Optimus 和 Agility Robotics 等公司免受大批量中国生产商的影响，这些生产商的机器人价格往往是美国竞争对手的一半或更低。 华盛顿对中国无人机和太阳能电池板实施了类似的限制，现在对中国电动汽车征收100%的关税。 这项禁令被广泛认为是特朗普试图争取时间，因为他对如何……措手不及。

reflection.en: In a world of rapid technological advancement and intense global competition, nations often take strategic steps to protect their interests and foster domestic innovation. Proverbs 27:12 reminds us of the wisdom in foreseeing potential dangers and taking prudent action. This trade decision reflects a nation's effort to secure its future position in a...
reflection.zh: 在科技飞速发展和全球竞争激烈的世界中，各国常采取战略措施来保护自身利益并促进国内创新。箴言27:12提醒我们，预见潜在危险并采取审慎行动是智慧之举。这项贸易决策反映了一个国家为确保其在关键新兴产业中的未来地位所做的努力。

verse.textEn: The prudent see danger and take refuge, but the simple keep going and pay the penalty.
verse.textZh: 通达人见祸藏躲；愚蒙人前往受害。

title.en: Small insects, big damage: The global ant trade is booming
title.zh: 小昆虫，大破坏：全球蚂蚁贸易正在蓬勃发展

summary.en: The global trade in African ants, both legal and illegal, is experiencing a significant boom. Hobbyists are drawn to these insects, but concerns are rising about the ecological risks this trade poses to various ecosystems, including the potential for power outages.
summary.zh: 非洲蚂蚁的全球贸易，无论合法与否，正在蓬勃发展。尽管爱好者们对这些昆虫趋之若鹜，但人们越来越担心这种贸易对生态系统造成的生态风险，其中甚至包括可能导致停电。

body.en:
Legal or not, the trade in African ants bound for Europe is booming. What do hobbyists find appealing about these insects, and what risks does the trade pose to ecosystems, including power outages?

They are unusual pieces of evidence that regularly appear in Kenyan  courtrooms: thousands of ants packed into tiny containers.

Since 2025, such finds have been presented in court several times. Staff from the Kenya Wildlife Service discovered them during baggage inspections. In multiple cases, they identified thousands of specimens of the sought-after Messor Cephalotes species also known as the Giant African Harvester Ant . A single queen can fetch more than €200 ($230) on the market.

The export of wild animals is generally prohibited in Kenya. Due to high levels of poaching — particularly involving elephants and rhinoceroses — many African countries have introduced tough laws against wildlife trafficking.

Kenya has also tightened its legislation. Under these rules, a Chinese  national who attempted to export ants was sentenced last April to one year in prison for biopiracy. Given the growing scale of smuggling and its ecological consequences , the judge said the sentence should serve as a deterrent.

It was already the second major ant-smuggling case in 12 months. The previous year, the wildlife service stopped four men who referred to themselves as the "Ant Gang." Among them were two 19-year-old Belgians  who were trying to smuggle 5,500 queens to Europe. They were fined around €5,000 each.

Whenever such cases arise, authorities often call entomologist Dino Martins to the airport. "I was shocked," he said. "Not only by the sheer number of ants, but also because they were queen ants."

The seized insects were young queens that had been dug up from nests in the ground, according to Martins, who has led several research institutes in Kenya and is regarded as one of Africa's leading ant experts, These queens have wings that allow them to fly away and establish new colonies.

"When you collect queens at this critical moment, you interrupt a key stage in the creation of new colonies," he said, adding that Kenya's ecosystems are also affected because ants transport grass seeds, helping to regenerate the savannah.

In Europe, keeping ants as pets has become increasingly popular, particularly among young people. Colonies are housed in glass terrariums where a queen produces offspring and establishes an entirely new population.

One person who keeps ants as a hobby is Michael Meier, who asked not to be identified by his real name. While at university, he wanted a pet that required little attention.

"With ants, it doesn't really matter whether I feed them today or tomorrow," he said.

At one point, Meier kept almost 30 colonies in a...
body.zh: 无论合法与否，运往欧洲的非洲蚂蚁贸易正在蓬勃发展。爱好者们对这些昆虫有何吸引力？这种贸易对生态系统造成了哪些风险，包括停电？ 它们是肯尼亚法庭上经常出现的不寻常证据：数千只蚂蚁被装在小容器里。 自 2025 年以来，此类调查结果已多次提交法庭。肯尼亚野生动物管理局的工作人员在行李检查时发现了它们。在多个案例中，他们鉴定了数千个备受追捧的 Messor Cephalotes 物种（也称为巨型非洲收割蚁）的标本。单个蜂王在市场上的售价可以超过 200 欧元（230 美元）。 肯尼亚普遍禁止出口野生动物。由于偷猎现象严重（特别是涉及大象和犀牛），许多非洲国家都出台了严厉的法律来打击野生动物贩运。 肯尼亚还加强了立法。根据这些规定，去年四月，一名试图出口蚂蚁的中国公民因生物剽窃被判处一年监禁。鉴于走私规模不断扩大及其对生态造成的影响，法官表示，该判决应起到威慑作用。 这已是12个月内第二起重大蚂蚁走私案。去年，野生动物服务部门拦住了四名自称“蚂蚁帮”的男子。其中有两名 19 岁的比利时人，他们试图将 5,500 名王后走私到欧洲。他们每人被罚款约 5,000 欧元。 每当出现此类情况时，当局通常会叫昆虫学家迪诺·马丁斯到机场。 “我很震惊，”他说。 “不仅因为蚂蚁的数量庞大，还因为它们是蚁后。” 马丁斯表示，被查获的昆虫是从地下巢穴中挖出来的年轻蚁后。马丁斯曾领导过肯尼亚多家研究机构，被认为是非洲领先的蚂蚁专家之一。这些蚁后拥有翅膀，可以让它们飞走并建立新的蚁群。 他说：“当你在这个关键时刻收集蚁后时，你就中断了新蚁群创建的关键阶段。”他补充说，肯尼亚的生态系统也会受到影响，因为蚂蚁会运输草籽，帮助大草原的再生。 在欧洲，饲养蚂蚁作为宠物越来越受欢迎，尤其是在年轻人中。蜂群被安置在玻璃容器中，蜂王在那里产下后代并建立一个全新的种群。 迈克尔·梅尔 (Michael Meier) 是一位以饲养蚂蚁为爱好的人，他要求不透露自己的真实姓名。在大学期间，他想要一只不需要太多照顾的宠物。 “对于蚂蚁来说，我今天或明天喂它们并不重要，”他说。 迈尔曾一度在一个……中饲养了近 30 个菌落。

reflection.en: The booming global trade in ants, with its potential for ecosystem damage and even power outages, reminds us that the earth and its intricate systems belong to Yahweh. Our actions, even in seemingly small hobbies, can have far-reaching consequences when we forget our role as caretakers of His creation. This calls us to consider the broader impact of our...
reflection.zh: 全球蚂蚁贸易的蓬勃发展，及其对生态系统乃至电力供应可能造成的巨大破坏，提醒我们大地和其中一切的丰盛都属于雅伟。我们的行为，即使是看似微小的爱好，当我们忘记自己作为祂受造物的看护者角色时，也可能产生深远的影响。这促使我们思考自己的欲望对雅伟所托付的自然界造成的更广泛影响。

verse.textEn: The earth is Yahweh's, and everything in it, the world, and all who live in it.
verse.textZh: 地和其中所充满的，世界和住在其间的，都属雅伟。

title.en: India's 'Cockroach' protesters face ongoing legal pressure
title.zh: 印度“蟑螂”抗议者面临持续的法律压力

summary.en: After forcing the resignation of India's education minister, student activists say a crackdown continues despite government promises to drop criminal cases against protesters.
summary.zh: 印度学生活动家表示，尽管政府承诺撤销针对抗议者的刑事案件，但在迫使印度教育部长辞职后，镇压仍在继续。

body.en:
After forcing the resignation of India's education minister, student activists say a crackdown continues despite government promises to drop criminal cases against protesters.

A student-led protest movement in India satirically called the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) scored a major political win when Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan stepped down after weeks of protests calling for his removal.

The movement began on social media as an activist campaign sparked by leaks of a question sheet for the NEET exam, a highly competitive entrance test for aspiring medical students, in early May.

Along with the education minister stepping down , the government promised to withdraw police cases against peaceful protesters, compensate families affected by the NEET examination controversy and continue talks on the movement's five-point charter for reforming India's examination system .

Now, student leaders, lawyers and activists say the battle has shifted from the streets to police stations, courtrooms and social media.

Indian lawyer and politician Kapil Sibal told DW that the government's actions after the movement called off further protests have raised fresh questions about whether its public assurances are being honored.

"The way Dharmendra Pradhan was celebrated after his resignation shows the government has learned nothing from the protests or the message the students were trying to convey," Sibal said.

The agreement that ended the protests appeared straightforward. Governments in Delhi, Bihar, Assam, Maharashtra and West Bengal announced that protest-related police cases would be withdrawn and detained students released.

But some of those orders included an important caveat. The protection does not extend to protesters whom police describe as having "criminal antecedents," a condition that student leaders say was never discussed during negotiations.

Senior advocate Rebecca Mammen John told DW that government assurances alone do not automatically end criminal proceedings.

"There is a prescribed legal process for withdrawing criminal cases. An oral assurance from the government counts for nothing unless that process is followed," John said.

"Ultimately, it is the courts that decide whether prosecutions are withdrawn or whether police cases are closed."

For the CJP, that legal distinction has become a new battleground. Its leaders argue the "criminal antecedents" clause risks leaving room for selective prosecution even after the movement agreed to suspend its protests.

Government officials, meanwhile, insist peaceful protesters have nothing to fear and that investigations will continue only against those accused of violence or other criminal offenses.

title.en: UK court allows plans for Chinese 'super' embassy to advance
title.zh: 英国法院批准中国“超级”大使馆建设计划

summary.en: A UK court has dismissed a legal challenge against Beijing's new embassy in London, which is set to become the largest in the UK. The case, brought by a neighborhood association, had cited security concerns regarding the embassy's presence.
summary.zh: 英国一家法院驳回了针对中国驻伦敦新大使馆的法律挑战，该大使馆建成后将成为英国最大的使馆。此案由一个社区协会提起，理由是该大使馆构成安全威胁。

body.en:
A court dismissed a legal challenge against Beijing's new embassy in London, which could become the largest in the UK. The case, brought by a neighborhood association, argued the embassy poses a security threat.

A UK High Court on Friday threw out a challenge against UK authorities' decision to permit a new Chinese super embassy in central London .

The challenge was brought by a neighborhood group called the Royal Mint Court Residents' Association (RMCRA), which represents families and businesses in roughly 100 properties around the planned embassy site.

The RMCRA argued the presence of the embassy could increase the risk of terrorist attacks, lead to the targeting of dissidents and be used to enforce "draconian" Chinese laws in the UK.

The association also claimed that the embassy could pose a fire risk, arguing that Chinese authorities might ignore safety obligations that would be difficult to enforce because of diplomatic immunity on the embassy site.

On that basis, the group argued the development should not have been approved by the UK government as well as the London Borough of Tower Hamlets.

Yet in its ruling on Friday, the High Court said the "RMCRA ​did not produce reasonable ⁠and convincing evidence of the likelihood that a violation of human rights ⁠affecting them ​personally would occur."

In a move that was widely seen as a goodwill gesture toward Beijing, the embassy received approval from the UK government shortly before then-Prime Minister Keir Starmer visited China in January this year. 

 If completed, the new Chinese embassy would be the largest embassy in the UK .

Beijing plans to build the embassy on the site of the former Royal Mint, next to the Tower of London. The site covers around 20,000 square meters (235,000 square feet).

Beijing purchased the property in 2018 for a reported $327 million (€283.9 million), with the intent of relocating its embassy there from its current premises in Portland Place.

In response to the verdict, the RMCRA said it would seek permission to appeal, hoping to take the case to the UK Supreme Court.

"Beijing thinks this judgment is the final word. It isn't. The appeal is already in the works," Luke Pollard, head of the RMCRA, said in a statement.

Activists from  Hong Kong's pro-democracy movement living in exile have also been skeptical of the project, telling DW they fear the embassy could help Beijing suppress dissidents abroad. 

The UK is home to the world's largest Hong Kong diaspora, with an estimated 285,000 people of Hong Kong origin living in the country.

title.en: From petitions to memes: How students made dissent visible
title.zh: 从请愿到网络迷因：学生如何让异议显现

summary.en: Student movements throughout history, from imperial China to modern India, have consistently found new ways to express dissent and challenge established authority, adapting their methods to contemporary tools and symbols.
summary.zh: 从中国古代到当今印度，学生运动不断调整其工具和象征，以挑战权威，使异议得以显现。

body.en:
From imperial China to present-day India, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols of their age to challenge authority.

On July 22, 2026, in rainy Mumbai, India , a casually dressed young woman stepped in front of a slow-moving police van carrying detained students. She placed her palm on the hood, forcing the vehicle to stop.

Mobile phones captured the moment from every angle. She too, raised her own phone and recorded the encounter. Within hours, the clip spread across India and beyond.

It became one of the defining visuals of the Cockroach Janta Party protests, a movement in which students demanded transparency and accountability, following leaks in India's medical entrance exams.

But the power of the moment lay not only in what she did, but in how quickly it was seen. A single gesture, a young woman confronting authority , became a symbol shared across millions of screens.

While the clip belongs to a generation raised on social media, the impulse behind it is much older.

From court petitions and revolutionary posters to photographs, umbrellas and memes, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols available to them, turning them into vehicles for dissent.

Long before television or social media carried dissent across borders, students still found ways to make their grievances heard.

In Eastern Han China, for instance, scholars at the Imperial Academy (Taixue) aligned with reform-minded officials in opposing powerful eunuchs at court, whom many viewed as corrupt and politically overbearing.

They voiced their objections through public criticism, political networks and petitions.

In an era when political communication moved through official channels, petitions were among the established ways of bringing grievances before the throne. Written in formal language and delivered through the bureaucracy, they carried student concerns directly into the state's communication system.

In Paris in 1968, students challenged university authorities and a conservative postwar social order. As demonstrations spread across the French capital and drew in workers, one of the movement's most enduring contributions emerged from a basement workshop at the Ecole des Beaux-Arts.

The Atelier Populaire ("People's Workshop") printed thousands of posters during the protests, many of them overnight. Their bold graphics, silhouettes and slogans became the visual language of the movement. Produced collectively, many carried no individual author's name, helping transform protest into a shared public voice.

The posters and their messages could appear in dozens of places overnight, giving the protest a wide local visual presence.

Protests also became more impactful when images could be transmitted across borders.

body.zh: 在日益脆弱的劳动力市场中，全国各地的工人们都担心人工智能会对他们的生计产生影响。在武汉绿树成荫的街道上，汽车与轻便摩托车和货运卡车争夺空间，最近一种新型车辆的故障导致该市道路出现混乱。三月份，无人驾驶出租车车队中的几辆车突然停在街上。 “系统故障”让心疼的乘客滞留了几个小时。这辆名为 Apollo Go 的机器人出租车由人工智能 (AI) 驱动，已被带离武汉街道数月以进行调查。继续阅读...

reflection.en: As technological advancements like AI reshape the world of work, it's natural for people to feel anxious about their livelihoods. This verse reminds us that all our labor, when done with diligence and integrity, can be an offering to Yahweh, giving it enduring purpose beyond economic shifts. Even as job roles evolve, the dignity of human contribution...
reflection.zh: 随着人工智能等技术进步重塑工作世界，人们对生计感到焦虑是自然的。这节经文提醒我们，我们所有的劳动，只要勤勉正直地完成，都可以是献给雅伟的供物，使其超越经济变迁而拥有持久的意义。即使工作角色不断演变，人类贡献的尊严依然存在，植根于更高的呼召。

verse.textEn: Whatever you do, work at it with all your heart, as working for Yahweh, not for human masters.
verse.textZh: 无论做什么，都要从心里做，像是给主做的，不是给人做的。

title.en: The future of AI hinges on openness and cooperation. China and Britain can gain much by working together | Zheng Zeguang
title.zh: 人工智能的未来取决于开放与合作。中英两国携手合作可获益良多 | 郑泽光

summary.en: The Chinese ambassador to the UK, Zheng Zeguang, argues that the future of artificial intelligence depends on international openness and cooperation between nations like China and Britain. He emphasizes the significant benefits to be gained through collaborative efforts in areas such as manufacturing, healthcare,...
summary.zh: 中国驻英国大使郑泽光指出，人工智能的未来取决于中英等国之间的国际开放与合作。他强调，通过在制造业、医疗、研究和治理等领域的协作，可以获得巨大的利益，并认为孤立竞争毫无意义。

body.en: There is no point competing in isolation. There are so many benefits to be had, in manufacturing, healthcare, research and governance Zheng Zeguang is the Chinese ambassador to the UK Artificial intelligence is widely regarded as one of the defining technologies of our time. Like the steam engine, the harnessing of electricity and the internet before it, it has the potential to transform how we work, live and interact. But every technological revolution brings challenges as well as opportunities. As AI systems become more capable, people are asking legitimate questions. How can AI remain safe, accountable and under human control ? How should its development be governed? How can its benefits be shared more widely? Continue reading...
body.zh: 孤立地竞争是没有意义的。在制造、医疗保健、研究和治理方面有很多好处。郑泽光是中国驻英国大使人工智能被广泛认为是我们这个时代的决定性技术之一。就像蒸汽机、电力和互联网的利​​用一样，它有可能改变我们的工作、生活和互动方式。但每一次技术革命都带来挑战和机遇。随着人工智能系统变得越来越强大，人们提出了合理的问题。人工智能如何保持安全、负责任并处于人类控制之下？其发展又该如何治理？如何让更广泛的人分享其好处？继续阅读...

reflection.en: The call for international cooperation in AI development echoes the wisdom that collective counsel brings strength and security. When nations work together, sharing insights and resources, they can navigate complex challenges and unlock greater benefits for all. This collaborative spirit, rather than isolated competition, reflects a path of shared wisdom...
reflection.zh: 呼吁在人工智能发展中进行国际合作，这与“谋士众多，人便安居”的智慧不谋而合。当各国携手合作，分享见解和资源时，它们就能应对复杂的挑战，为所有人带来更大的利益。这种协作精神，而非孤立竞争，体现了共享智慧和共同繁荣的道路。

verse.textEn: For lack of guidance a nation falls, but victory is won through many advisers.
verse.textZh: 无智谋，民就败落；谋士多，人便安居。

title.en: Anthony Fauci’s diaries take aim at News Corp journalist Sharri Markson’s ‘nonsense’ Covid-19 investigation
title.zh: 安东尼·福奇日记抨击新闻集团记者沙里·马克森的“胡说八道”新冠疫情调查

summary.en: Former US top health official Dr. Anthony Fauci's diaries reveal his dismissal of journalist Sharri Markson's COVID-19 origin investigation as 'nonsense.' Fauci, who was subpoenaed to appear at a Senate hearing on the virus, stated that Markson's reporting 'does not make any sense.'
summary.zh: 美国前首席卫生官员安东尼·福奇的日记显示，他驳斥记者沙里·马克森对新冠病毒起源的调查为“胡说八道”。福奇曾被传唤出席参议院关于该病毒的听证会，他表示马克森的报道“毫无道理”。

body.en: US former top health official, who was subpoenaed to appear at a Senate hearing into Covid-19, says Markson’s reporting about virus’s origin ‘does not make any sense’ Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Dr Anthony Fauci , the US’s chief medical adviser at the start of the pandemic, has described a book by News Corp investigative journalist Sharri Markson backing the “lab leak” theory of Covid-19’s origins as a “bunch of nonsense” in his newly released diaries. This week, Fauci, 85, was subpoenaed by the Republican senator Rand Paul to appear at a Senate hearing into Covid-19 and his handling of the pandemic. Continue reading...
body.zh: 被传唤出席参议院关于 Covid-19 的听证会的美国前高级卫生官员表示，马克森关于病毒起源的报道“没有任何意义”。 大流行开始时，美国首席医疗顾问安东尼·福奇博士将新闻集团调查记者莎莉·马克森 (Sharri Markson) 的一本支持 Covid-19 起源“实验室泄露”理论的书描述为在他新发表的日记中，“一堆废话”。本周，85 岁的福奇接到共和党参议员兰德·保罗的传票，出席参议院关于 Covid-19 及其处理疫情的听证会。继续阅读...

reflection.en: In public discourse, especially when complex issues like a pandemic's origins are debated, it is wise to consider all perspectives. As Proverbs 18:17 reminds us, the first account often seems right until another view is presented and examined. This encourages us to seek understanding from various sources before forming conclusions.
reflection.zh: 在公共讨论中，尤其当涉及疫情起源等复杂议题时，倾听各方观点是明智之举。正如箴言18:17提醒我们，先陈述案情的人似乎有理，直到另一方前来查问。这鼓励我们在下结论之前，从不同来源寻求理解。

verse.textEn: In a lawsuit the first to speak seems right, until someone comes forward and cross-examines.
verse.textZh: 先诉情由的，似乎有理；但邻舍来到，就察出实情。

title.en: BMW to cut ‘as many as 8,000 jobs’ under pressure from Chinese rivals
title.zh: 宝马在中国竞争对手的压力下将裁员“多达8,000人”

summary.zh: 据报道，宝马计划在德国的行政和开发部门裁员多达8,000人。此举是这家欧洲汽车制造商在中国竞争对手日益增长的压力下，为削减成本而采取的措施。

The Munich-headquartered company has started a voluntary redundancy programme agreed with employee representatives, a BMW spokesperson said on Wednesday. Continue reading...
body.zh: 德国的管理和开发部门将进行裁员，但生产运营不受影响 据报道，宝马计划在德国裁员多达 8,000 人，这是欧洲最大汽车制造商在中国竞争对手压力下削减成本的最新迹象。宝马发言人周三表示，这家总部位于慕尼黑的公司已启动与员工代表商定的自愿裁员计划。继续阅读...

Ecclesiastes 3:1 reminds us that "For everything there is a season, and a time for every matter under heaven." This perspective can help us acknowledge the difficult realities of transition, trusting that even amidst disruption, Yahweh's overarching...
reflection.zh: 宝马裁员的消息凸显了经济变革和全球竞争带来的挑战性季节。传道书3:1提醒我们：“凡事都有定期，天下万务都有定时。”这种视角能帮助我们认识到过渡时期的艰难现实，相信即使在动荡之中，雅伟的宏伟计划也涵盖了生命的所有季节。

verse.textEn: There is a time for everything, and a season for every activity under the heavens.

title.en: Where Australia sits in this $6 billion race for influence as China's strategy shifts
title.zh: 澳大利亚在这场60亿美元的影响力竞争中处于何种位置，中国战略正在转变

summary.en: A new report indicates that China's strategic influence in the Pacific region, which was once significant, has recently diminished. This shift is noted amidst a broader competition for influence involving countries like Australia.
summary.zh: 一份新报告指出，中国在太平洋地区曾拥有的“真正立足点”已有所缩小。这一变化是在澳大利亚等国更广泛的地区影响力竞争中被观察到的。

body.en:
Australia has continued to outrank China as the Pacific's biggest source of development aid, contributing a third of loans and infrastructure investment to the region, according to a new report.

Looking at development projects across the Pacific between 2008 and 2024, the Lowy Institute report found that, after years of decline, aid to the region increased by 10 per cent in 2024.

Total development aid stood at US$4.1 billion ($5.85 billion) in that year, but the report's authors estimate that would drop to US$3.8 billion ($5.42 billion) in yet-to-be-released 2025 figures.

With China now shifting strategy from big debt-fuelled loans to smaller strategic aid, and amid major economic shocks in the Pacific, the contest for regional influence is coming under greater strain.

Australia was the Pacific's biggest donor in 2024, giving $2.14 billion in aid, which made up 37 per cent of all finance to the region in that year.

A total of $6 billion in financing was dispensed from New Zealand, China, and regional development banks.

Australia has also inked $3.4 billion in loan deals, ending China's reign as the region's leading lender.

"That's a product of many years of Australia pushing into these spaces, but it's meant that what was once a real foothold for China in the region has been narrowed," the report's lead author Riley Duke told SBS News.

"Australia is consistently providing the most grant financing to the region, and that picture hasn't really changed."

The report, released on Tuesday, says demand for Chinese loans has dropped since 2019 due to concerns about servicing the debt, more competition between lenders and Chinese banks' capital availability.

Australia is also a major financier of climate change mitigation projects in the Pacific, including a solar and battery storage facility for Palau to help generate 20 per cent of its electricity, and Tonga's Renewable Energy Stabilisation Package.

The fruits of those efforts have paid off for Australia, with a flurry of regional security deals announced in recent months, including with Fiji, Vanuatu , Papua New Guinea and Tuvalu.

"They are a clear marker of Australia establishing itself as the lead partner to the region," Duke said.

"Those deals ... take a long time to progress. They're complicated, but they reflect Australia establishing itself as an inalienably important partner to Pacific countries."

Developing Pacific Island nations have been hit hard by multiple shocks, including the COVID-19 pandemic and more recently, fuel supply shortages caused by the United States-Israeli war on Iran.

Duke said these multiple challenges put the region at risk of...
body.zh: 一份新报告显示，澳大利亚继续超过中国，成为太平洋地区最大的发展援助来源国，为该地区贡献了三分之一的贷款和基础设施投资。 洛伊研究所的报告审视了 2008 年至 2024 年间太平洋地区的发展项目，发现在经历了多年的下降之后，对该地区的援助在 2024 年增加了 10%。 该年的发展援助总额为 41 亿美元（58.5 亿美元），但报告作者估计，在尚未公布的 2025 年数据中，这一数字将降至 38 亿美元（54.2 亿美元）。 随着中国目前的战略从大规模债务驱动的贷款转向规模较小的战略援助，并且在太平洋地区遭受重大经济冲击的情况下，争夺地区影响力的竞争正面临更大的压力。 2024年，澳大利亚是太平洋地区最大的捐助国，提供了21.4亿美元的援助，占当年该地区所有资金的37%。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 新西兰、中国和地区开发银行总共提供了 60 亿美元的融资。 澳大利亚还签署了 34 亿美元的贷款协议，结束了中国作为该地区主要贷款国的统治地位。 该报告的主要作者莱利·杜克 (Riley Duke) 告诉 SBS 新闻：“这是澳大利亚多年来进军这些领域的结果，但这意味着中国在该地区曾经真正的立足点已经缩小。” “澳大利亚一直在向该地区提供最多的赠款融资，这种情况并没有真正改变。” 周二发布的报告称，自 2019 年以来，对中国贷款的需求有所下降，原因是对偿债的担忧、贷款机构之间的竞争加剧以及中资银行的可用资本。 澳大利亚还是太平洋地区气候变化减缓项目的主要资助者，其中包括为帕劳建设一个太阳能和电池存储设施，帮助其发电20%，以及汤加的可再生能源稳定计划。 这些努力的成果为澳大利亚带来了回报，近几个月宣布了一系列区域安全协议，其中包括与斐济、瓦努阿图、巴布亚新几内亚和图瓦卢的协议。 杜克说：“它们是澳大利亚确立其作为该地区主要合作伙伴地位的明显标志。” “这些协议……需要很长时间才能取得进展。它们很复杂，但它们反映了澳大利亚将自己确立为太平洋国家不可分割的重要合作伙伴。” 太平洋发展中岛国受到多重冲击的严重打击，包括新冠肺炎 (COVID-19) 大流行以及最近美国和以色列对伊朗的战争造成的燃料供应短缺。 杜克表示，这些多重挑战使该地区面临……的风险。

reflection.en: In the complex "race for influence" among nations, strategic decisions are paramount. Proverbs reminds us that without wise guidance, a nation can falter, but with many counselors, there is security. This highlights the importance of thoughtful, well-advised leadership in navigating international relations and securing a nation's future.
reflection.zh: 在各国之间复杂的“影响力竞争”中，战略决策至关重要。箴言提醒我们，没有明智的指导，国家就会衰落；但有许多谋士，就能获得安全。这突显了在处理国际关系和确保国家未来方面，深思熟虑、听取良好建议的领导力的重要性。

verse.textEn: For lack of guidance a nation falls, but victory is won through many advisers.
verse.textZh: 无智谋，民就败落；谋士多，人便安居。

title.en: US-China AI rivalry heats up as Chinese models gain ground
title.zh: 中美人工智能竞争加剧，中国模型迎头赶上

summary.en: China's AI platforms are rapidly advancing, narrowing the gap with US technology. This progress has led to renewed threats from the Trump administration, alongside accusations of intellectual property theft, raising concerns about escalating tensions between the two nations.
summary.zh: 中国的人工智能平台正迅速缩小与美国同行的差距。这一进展引发了特朗普政府新的威胁，并伴随着知识产权盗窃的指控，令人担忧两国之间的紧张关系可能升级。

body.en:
China's AI platforms are rapidly closing the gap with their US counterparts, prompting fresh threats from the Trump administration. With accusations of intellectual property theft, could tensions boil over?

In what seems like the blink of an eye,  China has gone from being up to five years behind the United States in top-tier artificial intelligence (AI) to lagging by just a few months.

While US players, including Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's ChatGPT , have spent hundreds of billions of dollars to push the frontier of AI, China has pursued a very different path .

Faced with US curbs on high-end chips that help AI to do its most advanced thinking, Chinese tech firms have prioritized dozens of open-source AI models built on "good enough"  technology .

These platforms, including DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen and Xiaomi's MiMo, are now widely deployed across Chinese businesses, government services and consumer devices.

In the latest sign of the gap closing, Chinese startup Moonshot AI last week unveiled Kimi K3, a model that rivals one of the most advanced AI models — Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 — on key benchmarks.

In some tests, Kimi K3 matches or even surpasses Claude with far less computing power and at a fraction of the cost. 

Global technology specialist Alvin W. Graylin thinks Kimi K3's arrival turns high-end AI from an expensive luxury into something practical and affordable.

"For 98% of customers, the 1 to 2% difference [in knowledge] isn't worth paying 10 to 20 times more."

China's latest advance has already drawn a strong reaction from Washington, with US President Donald Trump now threatening to block US access to Chinese AI models.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, meanwhile, warned earlier this week that the US could sanction Chinese models over alleged intellectual property (IP) theft.

Anthropic  and OpenAI have accused Chinese labs of using their models to train their own systems, a process known as distilling.

While distilling is a common practice by AI labs worldwide to a limited extent, the companies say their models have been bombarded with queries to harvest advanced reasoning. The White House warned in April that China was doing it on an "industrial scale."

Beijing has hit back, rejecting the accusations as baseless and calling US threats of sanctions and model bans "technological bullying" to contain China's rise.

Giulia Neaher, a research analyst at the Strategic Foresight Hub at the Washington-based Stimson Center think tank, downplayed the role of distilling in Kimi's progress.

"A great degree [of its success] is due to the talent, infrastructure and the resources that were poured into building this...
body.zh: 中国的人工智能平台正在迅速缩小与美国同行的差距，引发了特朗普政府的新威胁。随着知识产权盗窃的指控，紧张局势会升级吗？ 似乎一眨眼的功夫，中国在顶级人工智能 (AI) 领域就从落后美国五年变为仅落后几个月。 尽管包括 Anthropic 的 Claude 和 OpenAI 的 ChatGPT 在内的美国企业已经花费了数千亿美元来推动人工智能的前沿发展，但中国却走了一条截然不同的道路。 面对美国对帮助人工智能实现最先进思维的高端芯片的限制，中国科技公司优先考虑了数十种基于“足够好”技术的开源人工智能模型。 这些平台，包括 DeepSeek、阿里巴巴的 Qwen 和小米的 MiMo，现已广泛部署在中国企业、政府服务和消费设备中。 作为缩小差距的最新迹象，中国初创公司 Moonshot AI 上周推出了 Kimi K3，该模型在关键基准测试上可与最先进的人工智能模型之一——Anthropic 的 Claude Fable 5 相媲美。 在某些测试中，Kimi K3 可以与 Claude 相媲美甚至超过 Claude，但其计算能力却要低得多，而成本却只是 Claude 的一小部分。 全球技术专家 Alvin W. Graylin 认为 Kimi K3 的到来将高端人工智能从昂贵的奢侈品变成了实用且负担得起的东西。 “对于 98% 的客户来说，[知识] 1% 到 2% 的差异并不值得多付 10 到 20 倍的费用。” 中国的最新进展已经引起华盛顿的强烈反应，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普现在威胁要阻止美国使用中国的人工智能模型。 与此同时，财政部长斯科特·贝森特本周早些时候警告称，美国可能会因涉嫌盗窃知识产权而制裁中国模型。 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 指责中国实验室使用他们的模型来训练他们自己的系统，这一过程被称为蒸馏。 虽然提炼是全球人工智能实验室在一定程度上的常见做法，但这些公司表示，他们的模型已经受到查询的轰炸，以收获高级推理。白宫四月份警告说，中国正在以“工业规模”这样做。 北京方面予以反击，否认这些指控毫无根据，并称美国威胁实施制裁和示范禁令是“技术欺凌”，旨在遏制中国的崛起。 华盛顿智库史汀生中心战略远见中心的研究分析师朱莉娅·尼赫（Giulia Neaher）淡化了提炼在基米进步中的作用。 “[其成功]很大程度上归功于为建设这个项目而投入的人才、基础设施和资源......

reflection.en: In a world of intense technological competition and rising international tensions, the call to live peaceably with all people becomes profoundly relevant. Even amidst accusations and threats, seeking paths to de-escalation and mutual respect is vital for global stability. Yahweh's wisdom encourages us to pursue peace wherever possible, even when faced with...
reflection.zh: 在科技竞争激烈、国际关系日益紧张的世界中，与所有人和平相处的呼召变得至关重要。即使面对指控和威胁，寻求缓和局势和相互尊重的途径对全球稳定也至关重要。雅伟的智慧鼓励我们，即使面对竞争，也要尽可能追求和平。

title.en: El Niño is already here. But there's still a 'window of opportunity'
title.zh: 厄尔尼诺现象已至，但仍有“机会之窗”

summary.en: The El Niño climate pattern has arrived and is projected to be one of the strongest ever recorded, prompting questions about its potential impacts on Australians.
summary.zh: 厄尔尼诺气候模式已经到来，预计将成为有记录以来最强的一次，引发了人们对其可能对澳大利亚人造成影响的疑问。

body.en:
As El Niño strengthens, now is the "window of opportunity" to prepare before its potential impacts unfold, the World Meteorological Organisation (WMO) has warned.

The United Nations agency said El Niño is continuing to intensify and is expected to strengthen from August to October in a new long-range forecast released Saturday.

El Niño typically peaks between November and February, with its greatest influence on global temperatures often felt in the following year.

It's expected to drive up the likelihood of higher-than-normal temperatures across many parts of the world, increasing the risk of drought in some regions and wetter conditions in others.

"El Niño is not just on our doorstep — it is inside the house and turning up the heat," UN Secretary-General António Guterres said.

"And this is only a warm-up act. El Niño is strengthening — adding fuel to a planet already on fire with scorching heat domes, apocalyptic wildfires and record hot seas."

The World Food Programme is seeking to protect 8.8 million people across 22 high-risk countries before weather patterns "escalate into humanitarian emergencies". It expects parts of Africa, Central America and East Asia to be the most at risk.

In Australia, El Niño increases the likelihood of warmer and drier conditions, particularly in the east and southeast, raising the risk of drought and bushfires.

The Bureau of Meteorology (BoM) declared El Niño underway in mid-June, and forecasts it will be a "very strong event" — perhaps among the strongest observed since 1950 — that may persist into autumn next year.

WMO Secretary-General Celeste Saulo urged people and leaders around the world to consider the potential risks to their communities and take action.

"El Niño is one of the most closely monitored climate phenomena in the world," she said.

"This El Niño developing against the backdrop of unprecedented ocean heat and rising temperatures, provides governments and communities with a window of opportunity to anticipate risks and act before impacts unfold."

An El Niño declaration can be particularly concerning for farmers and those in bushfire-prone regions.

While it doesn't guarantee hotter and drier conditions, it does raise the probability that they will occur.

Andrew King, an associate professor of climate science at the University of Melbourne, said that while this El Niño is likely to be one of the strongest on record, a strong El Niño does not necessarily have a huge bearing on Australian climate compared to a weak one.

title.en: 'Mirage': Voice architect Noel Pearson breaks silence at Garma on referendum defeat
title.zh: “海市蜃楼”：原住民“议会之声”提案设计者诺埃尔·皮尔逊在加尔马节打破公投失败后的沉默

summary.en: Noel Pearson, a key architect of the proposed Indigenous Voice to Parliament, has delivered his first major public address since the referendum's defeat nearly three years ago, speaking at the Garma festival.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚原住民“议会之声”提案的主要设计者诺埃尔·皮尔逊在公投失败近三年后，首次在加尔马节上发表重要公开讲话。

body.en:
Noel Pearson, the architect of the failed Voice to Parliament 2023 referendum, has given his first major public speech in three years at this year's Garma Festival, Australia's largest Indigenous cultural gathering .

"For those of us who urged faith, hope and love, there is an account to be given for the hopes raised, the faith urged and the love lost in the referendum," he said.

"I must account for that. Three years later, I stand here with great reluctance.

"What right has anyone to raise hopes when those hopes were so badly misplaced? What right has anyone to offer a vision that turns out to be a mirage? That is the source of my hesitation to speak of these things. But I cannot allow the failure of the referendum to excuse me from my responsibility."

Nearly three years have passed since just over 60 per cent of Australians voted against enshrining an Indigenous Voice in the constitution, with every state and territory except the ACT rejecting the proposal.
